description_full: Chervon Holdings Limited, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the research, development, manufacture, testing, sale, and after-sale servicing of power tools, outdoor power equipment, and related products in North America, Europe, China, and internationally. It operates through Power Tools, Outdoor Power Equipment, and Others segments. The company offers power tools and accessories for consumer, professionals, and industrial users, as well as original design manufacturer (ODM) customers; and outdoor tools and its accessories for professional and mass-market users. It provides its products under the FLEX, DEVON, EGO, SKIL, X-TRON and ODM brand names. It is also involved in investment holding activities; trading and financial management; sale of parts and components to home appliances business; sale of do-it design, operation, and sale of do-it-yourself products; and production and sale of gardening tools. Chervon Holdings Limited was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Nanjing, China.

financial_summary: CHERVON HLDGS LTD. is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.9B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -6% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -2.2pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 32%.

The business throws off $156M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 10.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 76% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
